text.p: Turkish central bank injected a total of 43.85 trillion lira via overnight lending and an open market repo auction to relieve a continuing cash squeeze.

It gave 17.1 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent to banks after feeding 26.75 trillion lira through six-day repos in the morning at an average annual rate of 74.09 percent, up from 73.58 percent at Tuesday's seven-day repo auction.

Despite tight liquidity, the lira closed weaker at 93,175 to the dollar due to the U.S. currency's gains against the mark abroad and a higher central bank dollar rate for banks' forex transfers. Tuesday's close was 92,865.
The Turkish central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 93,000 lira at the opening, up from 92,750 at Tuesday's close.

Yields on the most heavily traded t-bills with 1997 maturity dived by between two and four percentage points after record bid and sale at Tuesday's 238-d t-bill auction. Yields on t-bills with 1996 maturity eased about one point.

The Treasury had sold a record 288.2 trillion lira worth t-bills yesterday after receiving bids reaching a record 480.6 trillion for the June 4 papers which had the longest maturity issued so far this year.
The average yield on June 4, which was sold at 130.72 percent average rate in the auction, dived to 127.51 percent.
The second most active April 9 paper yielded 122.63 percent, down from Tuesday's 124.74 percent average.
